org: Government of Canada — Aurora Design System (GCcollab / GCTools) data visualization
accessNotes: All eight Aurora data pages plus the colour and typography component pages were read as server-rendered HTML; example images downloaded from /static/. The guide does not define a dedicated chart palette (it says any colour meeting contrast is acceptable); the series colours listed are sampled from its example images and the Aurora/GCTools swatch families. Canada.ca / Statistics Canada guidance was not needed and not consulted.
summary: Aurora is the Government of Canada's GCTools design system; its data-viz guidance targets accessible web applications/dashboards. Charts are minimal and teal/slate-toned: a centred title-case Rubik title, both axes always titled, light dashed grey gridlines, a heavier blue-grey axis baseline, flat square-topped bars twice as wide as their gaps with value labels, and line series distinguished by both colour and hollow marker shape. Every visualisation must be accompanied by a raw data table, and legends are white shadowed cards.

colors.categoricalNotes: No prescribed chart palette: 'Any colour is acceptable for a visualization so long as it meets contrast requirements.' Use as little colour as possible; one designated colour per variable; multiple colours only for multiple variables, chosen as a complementary, distinguishable palette; avoid biased pairs such as red/green unless meaningful. Colours above are sampled from the guide's multi-line example (Series 1 slate #477c8e triangles, Series 2 light green #ade18d squares, Series 3 teal #43bdbc circles); single-series column example uses mint #55c0a3; area example slate line #467b8d. Aurora Borealis swatch family (GCTools main colours): #002D42, #137991, #6DD2DA, #15A3A6, #92CC6F. Canada.ca theme: #333000 (as printed), #26374A, #AF3C43, #F5F5F5, #FFFFFF. Thunder and Lightning: #002D42, #4D5D6C, #96A8B2, #CECECE, #FEC04F.
colors.notes: Text says 'Axis lines should use light grey (#E0E0E0)'; in the example images #E0E0E0 is used for the dashed gridlines while the x/y axis baselines are a heavier blue-grey (#96A8B2, sampled; same hex as the table border colour). Negative bars: same colour at 60% opacity. Area fill: line colour at 15% opacity. Stylized-number chevrons: decrease #923534, increase #2B542C. Table borders #96a8b2, striped/selected row fill #F2F5F6. All colours must meet WCAG AA (AAA ideal). Headings/text #252525 on light, #FFFFFF on dark.

typography.family: Rubik (titles, axis labels) + Nunito Sans (legend, body, sub-headings)
typography.fallback: Calibri or similar sans-serif; browser default font if web fonts blocked

axisTitle.placement: y title rotated 90° left of axis, x title centred well below the tick labels; both always present, outside the data area

typography.notes: Graph titles use Heading 2 (Rubik Regular 28pt/1.75em), title case; axis labels Heading 4 (Rubik Regular 21pt). Legend title 'Legend' Nunito Sans Regular 18px; legend items Nunito Sans Regular 16px. Table titles Heading 3 (Rubik Medium 24px, tracking 10); table headers Nunito Sans Bold 16px. Stylized numbers: Rubik Regular 125pt number, Heading 4 caption, Heading 5 percentage with chevron. Body text Nunito Sans 16/24. Example images render tick labels in Rubik at small size in near-black.

structure.gridlines: Light grey (#E0E0E0) dashed gridlines; horizontal in column charts; both horizontal and vertical in line/area charts ('lightening grids').
structure.axisLine: Left y-axis and bottom x-axis drawn as solid ~2–3px blue-grey (#96A8B2) lines.
structure.ticks: No visible tick marks; labels centred under ticks.
structure.yAxisTitle: rotated 90°, left of the tick labels
structure.unitPlacement: In the axis label: 'For quantitative labels, the unit of measurement should be included in the label.'
structure.frame: none around the plot; legends sit in white cards
structure.notes: Always include one additional increment above the data maximum (e.g. axis to 40 when max is 39). Consistent label intervals; skipping labels allowed. y labels 'left-aligned and kept above the y-axis lines' (per text). Long x labels rotated 45° from an origin directly below the tick.

legend.placement: side of the graph by default; bottom when there is a secondary axis
legend.directLabels: Prefer context on the chart; legends/tooltips only when absolutely necessary; never a legend for one data category.
legend.title: Card shows the word 'Legend' at top (Nunito Sans Regular 18px)
legend.swatchShape: line segment with the series' hollow marker shape (triangle, square, circle)
legend.notes: Legend card: white #FFFFFF rectangle, 4px radius, drop shadow 15% opacity 5px blur, padding 20×16px; items 16px Nunito Sans with 14px vertical padding (side) or inline items with 14×11px padding (bottom; 96px tall when one row). Don't rely on colour alone — use different shapes.

marks.bars: Bars twice as wide as the gap between them; never rounded tops; one colour per variable; negative bars same colour at 60% opacity; numerical values always shown beside bars. Prefer column (vertical) graphs; always columns when time is a variable; horizontal bars only for long labels or >10 items; 5–15 categories ideal.
marks.lines: Medium-weight straight segments with hollow white-filled markers in distinct shapes per series (triangle, square, circle); max three data sets per run chart; time on x-axis; at least ~20 data points ideal.
marks.areas: Fill = line colour at 15% opacity; lower opacity where series overlap; stacked area for part-to-whole.
marks.points: Scatterplots: vary opacity for overlapping clusters; trend lines only for strong correlations.
marks.notes: Stylized numbers (KPI): huge Rubik number, caption below offset left, % change with coloured chevron.

labels.dataLabels: 'Numerical values should always be shown beside visual elements' in bar/column graphs.
labels.numberFormat: Money abbreviations $1.2k, $3.4m, $6.2b (lowercase); avoid abbreviations otherwise; round-number increments.
labels.dates: Days: Mon, Tues, Wed, Thurs, Fri, Sat, Sun; months: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec; 12-hour time '1 a.m.', '2 p.m.'.

furniture.title: Short, title-case title reflecting the question the dataset answers; Heading 2; centred above the plot in examples.
furniture.other: A raw data table must accompany every visualisation (multiple formats). Tables: title Heading 3, 13px gap to table, header bottom border 2px #96a8b2, row borders 1px #96a8b2, 21×27px cell padding, striped rows #F2F5F6.

annotations: Tooltips only when necessary; example tooltip is a small dark-grey (#4c4c4c) box with white text '(40, Tues)' and a left-pointing arrow beside the hovered marker.
layout: If a graph is too complex, split into multiple simple graphs. Zoom on run charts recommended. Tables full container width.
interaction: Hover tooltip: dark grey rectangular label with pointer showing '(value, category)'. Interactive tables: sort icons, checkbox column (selected rows #F2F5F6), pagination, filters, search.
accessibility: All colours WCAG AA (AAA ideal); use textures as well as colour; distinct marker shapes per series; data table always available; sans-serif fonts for readability.

discouraged: more than three lines in a run chart
more than 15 categories in a bar/column chart
chartTypes.notes: If the data is easy to understand without a visualization, use a table.

distinctiveRules.rule: Bars are twice as wide as the gap between them (bar:gap = 2:1) with square (never rounded) tops.
distinctiveRules.quote: Bars should be twice as wide as the space between them. ... Graph bars should never have a rounded top.

distinctiveRules.rule: Negative bars use the same colour as positive bars at 60% opacity.
distinctiveRules.quote: Negative bars should use the same colour but at 60% opacity.

distinctiveRules.rule: Value labels always shown beside bars/columns.
distinctiveRules.quote: Numerical values should always be shown beside visual elements.

distinctiveRules.rule: Both axes always carry a title, placed outside the data area, with the unit included for quantitative axes.
distinctiveRules.quote: Both the x and y-axes should always be labeled. ... the unit of measurement should be included in the label.

distinctiveRules.rule: Chart title in title case (Rubik Regular 28pt, Heading 2), centred above the plot.
distinctiveRules.quote: Graph and table titles ... use the typography style for heading 2. ... Titles always use title-case capitalization.

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines light grey #E0E0E0 and dashed; axis baselines heavier blue-grey.
distinctiveRules.quote: Axis lines should use light grey (#E0E0E0), to not distract

distinctiveRules.rule: Value axis extends one increment beyond the data maximum.
distinctiveRules.quote: Always include an additional increment greater than the dataset.

distinctiveRules.rule: Long x labels rotated 45° from directly below their tick.
distinctiveRules.quote: Long text labels should be rotated 45 degrees around an origin directly below their corresponding axis tick.

distinctiveRules.rule: Line series distinguished by both colour and hollow marker shape (triangle, square, circle); max three lines.
distinctiveRules.quote: Do not have more than three data sets ... Using different shapes for data points will also help distinguish multiple variables

distinctiveRules.rule: Area fill = line colour at 15% opacity.
distinctiveRules.quote: Area graphs should be filled in with the same colour as the line, but at 15% opacity.

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend is a white card (4px radius, 15% shadow, 5px blur, 20×16px padding) titled 'Legend', placed at the side, or at the bottom when there is a secondary axis; never for a single series.
distinctiveRules.quote: Card component, rectangle (white, #FFFFFF) with a border radius of 4px, drop shadow with 15% opacity and 5px blur.

distinctiveRules.rule: Every chart is accompanied by a raw data table.
distinctiveRules.quote: a simple data table, or other ways of viewing the raw data, should be available somewhere on the page.

distinctiveRules.rule: Use column graphs whenever time is a variable; horizontal bars only for long labels or more than 10 items.
distinctiveRules.quote: If you are using time as a variable in your visualization, always use a column graph.

distinctiveRules.rule: Money abbreviated with lowercase suffixes ($1.2k, $3.4m, $6.2b); days abbreviated Mon, Tues, Wed, Thurs.

referenceImages.describes: Column chart template: centred 'Graph Title' in Rubik Regular black above the plot. Seven flat mint-green (#55c0a3) columns, square tops, bars about twice the gap width. Light grey dashed horizontal gridlines; heavy blue-grey (#99abb3) left y-axis and bottom x-axis; y ticks 0–40 left; category labels 'Unit' centred below; rotated y title 'Category Axis Title' and centred x title below. No legend, no source, white background.

Multi-line run chart Mon–Sun with three series: slate blue (#477c8e) with hollow triangles, light green (#ade18d) with hollow squares, teal (#43bdbc) with hollow circles; straight segments. Dashed light grey gridlines in both directions; heavy blue-grey axes; centred title 'Graph Title'; rotated y title; x title well below. A dark grey tooltip '(40, Tues)' with a left-pointing notch beside a hovered triangle.

Single-series area chart Jan–Dec: slate line (#467b8d) with small hollow circle markers, area filled in the same hue at ~15% opacity (#e3ebee). Dashed light gridlines both directions, heavy blue-grey axes, centred title, rotated 'Category Y-Axis Title' and 'Category X-Axis Title'.

Bottom-aligned legend card: white rectangle with soft shadow, 'Legend' label top-left, then inline items each with a short line segment through a hollow marker (triangle slate, square light green, circle teal) and labels 'Series 1/2/3'.
